452:
What's all this shouting? Who said you could go out?
- He's back... The bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish for
everything to be new for you this year.
455:
Anything may happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... Just a moment...
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him these days.
459:
What's to make sense of? He says
he'll find us anywhere and cut our throats.
461:
They say he slit Freckles' throat with a razor.
- He's gone savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's here to see you? Father Frost!
He's brought presents for you!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What have I done?
- Come on. Wear these in good health. They're slippers.
464:
- What do I need slippers for? I don't have a home.
- You will. You've got your whole life ahead.
465:
- They'll do in prison for now. Wear them.
- Always predicting the worst.
466:
These are for you, Vasya. And these
are for you, Gavrila Petrovich. - Thanks.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Must you get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and talk
heart to heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor, asking for a confession.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Find another sucker
to play cards with. You've got nine aces!
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you take the last letter, W:
"Warsaw." Then you say one beginning with W. Got it?
477: Your turn, Fedya. A city beginning with W.
478:
Vorkuta.
- Why? - I did time there.
479:
- All right. Yours begins with A, then.
- Dzhambul. - What has Dzhambul got to do with it?
480:
It's warm there. My home is there,
and my mother.
481:
Let's play this instead. I'll go out,
you hide something, and I'll find it.
482:
- Better if you found the helmet.
- Quiet.
483:
- We hide it, and he peeks through a hole?
- No. You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch to make sure I don't peek.
- Why me? It's always Fedya!
485:
- I'll rip your jaws off, you rascal!
- Always "jaws, jaws"...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Mean as a dog?
490:
- You came yourself.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried going to your place,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Just come.
495:
- Sorry to bother you needlessly, Doctor.
- Not at all.
496:
Give him valerian drops, warm tea,
and let him sleep. - Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, hello! We found out
that you were in prison,
500:
and were very glad,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
What rat told that Gloomy little kid
his dad was in prison?
502:
"Mom was glad too, because when
your letter came, she cried all day.
503:
Before that, she'd told us
you were a test pilot."
505:
"But I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506: you're a good man, but weak-willed."
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed. He stole our money
and blamed the cabbie.
508: Scram! I'll knock your horns off, radish!
510:
You should be ashamed! You're forty.
Half your life is behind you.
511:
What have you done? What do you have now?
What lies ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, nothing decent!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
513:
Listen, Docent. We'd better clear out.
The doctor will tell the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why?
- I, well... slit her throat with a razor.
515:
She's down the well.
See for yourself.
516: What was my sentence? One year.
518:
How much for the nursery
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
Should I put up with that monster
for a measly fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old lady down the well?
Do as you like. I'm going to the police.
522: Go ahead! He won't touch you.
523:
What about you? Will you put up with him
until he kills you?
524:
Vasya, the other day I told him
I'd caught a cold, and he...
525:
Enough about your cold! I'm sick of it.
Come here.
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades, the comedy is over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
I'll serve my sentence, then that's it.
I'm going straight. I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? A watchman at my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could clear snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought back that hat!
The Docent's just one crook of many,
534:
- but there's only one hat.
- The helmet would've cut our sentences.
535:
Where'd he put it?
We checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was "jaws, jaws."
537:
- He made me dive in that freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When we got caught. Remember?
He said he was fishing, and told me to dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing through a hole in the ice.
540:
Can you swim, Squint?"
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole!
541:
That's it! I remember, the bad man!
In the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you oaf?
You could've left a note before hanging yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Let them fetch him. I'm not carrying that great lump. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's on the bottom. Someone must dive.
546:
Why me? Every time, it's Squint.
Vasya, tell him to dive himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- You tried hanging yourself, and now you're afraid of a cold?
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd kill you, but I haven't got time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another one at the dacha.
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
